title: Direct current from cells and batteries
log: 2026-11-12T12:44:23Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: None of the bank points teaches direct current from cells or batteries; the closest, ocean currents, is about heat transport and the others are about cell biology, so the new point needs its own card.

draft.title: Direct current from cells and batteries
card: In direct current (DC), charge flows in one direction only. In alternating current (AC), the flow keeps reversing direction.
turns light energy straight into electrical energy as DC. It has no turbine and no moving magnet.
turns stored chemical energy into electrical energy as DC. It also has no turbine and no moving magnet.
Many devices, such as phones and torches, run on DC. A solar cell makes electricity while light falls on it. A battery makes it until its chemical energy runs low.
draft.remember: Solar cells and batteries give DC with no turbine: light or chemical energy in, electrical energy out.

a.q: A torch runs on batteries. Which energy change happens inside the batteries?
a.why: A battery supplies DC from stored chemical energy. Light to electrical is what a solar cell does, and the battery has no moving parts that turn kinetic energy into electricity.
a.clue: What is stored inside a battery before it is used?

b.q: Mia fits a small solar cell to a garden light in Bendigo. What does the cell supply to the light, and how?
opts: DC, by turning light directly into electricity
AC, by turning light directly into electricity
DC, by spinning a magnet inside a coil of wire
AC, by spinning a magnet inside a coil of wire
b.why: A solar cell turns light straight into DC, with no magnet or turbine. The spinning magnet and coil method makes AC, so it is wrong here, and a solar cell does not make AC.
b.clue: A solar cell has no moving parts.

b.best: DC, by turning light directly into electricity
